title: Is the UK abandoning its cities
titleChinese: 英国人“逃离”大城市的原因
paragraphs: We owe a lot to cities. These densely populated hubs of transit, industry and commerce brought together great swathes of the population. More than just living together for safety, cities allowed people to cooperate more easily and, as a result, develop more complex societies, science, and culture – things we continue to benefit from today.

In 2016 the UN revealed that over 50% of the world's population live in urban settlements. Of these cities, 31 are classified as megacities. A megacity is one where its inhabitants number more than 10 million. And globally this trend is expected to increase. London is no exception. Unsurprisingly, as England's capital city, London has a population of over 10 million – up by 1.1 million since 2008, according to one BBC article. This is a result of a higher birth rate than mortality rate, and an increase in international immigration. However, despite these rises, half a million more people have migrated away from this metropolis than have flocked to it. Why might this be?

It's the result of age. Where members of all other age groups tend to depart more than they arrive, young people between the ages of 20 and 30 are drawn to the range and number of jobs that the city offers and the education opportunities that can be found there. This explains why London has one of the youngest average populations in the UK, just 37, according to the BBC.

And the rest of the country? From 2002 to 2015 municipalities such as Liverpool, Birmingham and Manchester saw a population growth of 181%, 163% and 149% respectively, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Young professionals looking for high-paying jobs are attracted to the opportunities provided by growth in sectors such as finance and law. This in turn causes the development of city amenities such as gyms, restaurants and bars, making it an even more attractive place to live.

So are people in the UK leaving cities? It depends on where you look. What does seem clear is that people's views on the advantages of urban living may change as they get older. Where once was opportunity, now there may be hassle. Has your relationship with a city changed over time?

vocabulary.entry: owe a lot to /əʊ ə lɒt tu/ 亏欠……良多；受惠于……
vocabulary.example: We owe a lot to our parents for their unconditional love and support.
vocabulary.translation: 我们亏欠父母良多，感谢他们无条件的爱与支持。

vocabulary.entry: densely populated /ˈdensli ˈpɒpjuleɪtɪd/ 人口稠密的
vocabulary.example: This area is one of the most densely populated regions in the country.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区是这个国家人口最稠密的区域之一。

vocabulary.entry: hub /hʌb/ n. 枢纽；中心
vocabulary.example: This airport is an important transportation hub in the region.
vocabulary.translation: 这座机场是该地区重要的交通枢纽。

vocabulary.entry: commerce /ˈkɒmɜːs/ n. 商业；贸易
vocabulary.example: The city is a major center of commerce and industry.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市是重要的工商业中心。

vocabulary.entry: great swathes of /ɡreɪt sweɪðz ɒv/ 大片的；大量的
vocabulary.example: Great swathes of land have been turned into farmland.
vocabulary.translation: 大片土地被改造成了农田。

vocabulary.entry: urban settlements /ˈɜːbən ˈsetlmənts/ 城镇区域；城市聚居地
vocabulary.example: The government is investing in improving infrastructure in urban settlements.
vocabulary.translation: 政府正投入资金改善城镇区域的基础设施。

vocabulary.entry: megacity /ˈmeɡəsɪti/ n. 特大城市
vocabulary.example: Tokyo is one of the largest megacities in the world.
vocabulary.translation: 东京是全球最大的特大城市之一。

vocabulary.entry: inhabitant /ɪnˈhæbɪtənt/ n. 居民；住户
vocabulary.example: The inhabitants of the village are very friendly to tourists.
vocabulary.translation: 这个村子的居民对游客十分友好。

vocabulary.entry: mortality rate /mɔːˈtæləti reɪt/ 死亡率
vocabulary.example: The country has seen a steady decline in its mortality rate over the past decade.
vocabulary.translation: 过去十年间，这个国家的死亡率持续下降。

vocabulary.entry: international immigration /ˌɪntəˈnæʃnəl ˌɪmɪˈɡreɪʃn/ 国际移民
vocabulary.example: International immigration has contributed to the cultural diversity of the city.
vocabulary.translation: 国际移民促进了这座城市的文化多样性。

vocabulary.entry: metropolis /məˈtrɒpəlɪs/ n. 大都市；首府
vocabulary.example: New York is a bustling metropolis with a diverse population.
vocabulary.translation: 纽约是一座人口多元化的繁华大都市。

vocabulary.entry: flock to /flɒk tu/ 涌向；大批前往
vocabulary.example: Every year, tourists flock to this small town to enjoy its beautiful scenery.
vocabulary.translation: 每年都有大批游客涌向这座小镇，欣赏其美丽的风景。

vocabulary.entry: be drawn to /bi drɔːn tu/ 被……吸引
vocabulary.example: She was drawn to the job because of its flexible working hours.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作灵活的工作时间吸引了她。

vocabulary.entry: municipality /mjuːˌnɪsɪˈpæləti/ n. 城市；市政当局
vocabulary.example: The municipality has announced plans to build a new park.
vocabulary.translation: 市政当局已宣布要修建一座新公园的计划。

vocabulary.entry: respectively /rɪˈspektɪvli/ adv. 分别地；各自地
vocabulary.example: Tom and Jane scored 90 and 95 points respectively in the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 汤姆和简在考试中分别取得了90分和95分的成绩。

vocabulary.entry: young professional /jʌŋ prəˈfeʃənl/ 年轻职场人士；青年专业人才
vocabulary.example: The company is looking to hire young professionals with fresh ideas.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司希望招聘有新想法的年轻职场人士。

vocabulary.entry: sector /ˈsektə(r)/ n. 行业；领域
vocabulary.example: The technology sector is developing rapidly in this country.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家的科技行业发展迅速。

vocabulary.entry: in turn /ɪn tɜːn/ 反过来；依次
vocabulary.example: Economic growth will improve people's living standards, and this in turn will boost consumption.
vocabulary.translation: 经济增长会提高人们的生活水平，而这反过来又会刺激消费。

vocabulary.entry: amenity /əˈmiːnəti/ n. 公共设施；便利设施
vocabulary.example: The new residential area has a lot of amenities, including a swimming pool and a library.
vocabulary.translation: 这个新住宅区有很多配套设施，包括游泳池和图书馆。

vocabulary.entry: hassle /ˈhæsl/ n. 麻烦；烦心事
vocabulary.example: I don't want the hassle of moving house again.
vocabulary.translation: 我不想再经历搬家的麻烦了。

vocabulary.entry: cooperate /kəʊˈɒpəreɪt/ v. 合作；协作
vocabulary.example: The two companies decided to cooperate on the new project.
vocabulary.translation: 这两家公司决定就这个新项目展开合作。

vocabulary.entry: complex /ˈkɒmpleks/ adj. 复杂的；繁复的
vocabulary.example: The system is too complex for most people to understand.
vocabulary.translation: 这个系统太过复杂，大多数人都无法理解。

sentences.english: We owe a lot to cities.
sentences.chinese: 我们在很多方面受惠于城市。

sentences.english: These densely populated hubs of transit, industry and commerce brought together great swathes of the population.
sentences.chinese: 这些人口稠密的交通、工业和商业枢纽，汇聚了大量人口。

sentences.english: More than just living together for safety, cities allowed people to cooperate more easily and, as a result, develop more complex societies, science, and culture – things we continue to benefit from today.
sentences.chinese: 城市的意义不止于让人们为了安全聚居，更让人们得以更便捷地协作，进而发展出更复杂的社会、科学和文化——我们今天仍从中受益。

sentences.english: In 2016 the UN revealed that over 50% of the world's population live in urban settlements.
sentences.chinese: 2016年，联合国公布的数据显示，全球超过50%的人口居住在城镇区域。

sentences.english: Of these cities, 31 are classified as megacities.
sentences.chinese: 在这些城市中，有31座被归类为特大城市。

sentences.english: A megacity is one where its inhabitants number more than 10 million.
sentences.chinese: 特大城市指的是人口超过1000万的城市。

sentences.english: And globally this trend is expected to increase.
sentences.chinese: 而且从全球范围来看，这一趋势预计还会持续加剧。

sentences.english: London is no exception.
sentences.chinese: 伦敦也不例外。

sentences.english: Unsurprisingly, as England's capital city, London has a population of over 10 million – up by 1.1 million since 2008, according to one BBC article.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司的一篇报道称，作为英格兰的首都，伦敦人口已超过1000万，自2008年以来增长了110万，这一结果并不出人意料。

sentences.english: This is a result of a higher birth rate than mortality rate, and an increase in international immigration.
sentences.chinese: 人口增长得益于出生率高于死亡率，以及国际移民数量的增加。

sentences.english: However, despite these rises, half a million more people have migrated away from this metropolis than have flocked to it.
sentences.chinese: 然而，尽管人口出现增长，从这座大都市迁出的人口还是比涌入的人口多出了50万。

sentences.english: Why might this be?
sentences.chinese: 这背后的原因是什么呢？

sentences.english: It's the result of age.
sentences.chinese: 这是由年龄因素造成的。

sentences.english: Where members of all other age groups tend to depart more than they arrive, young people between the ages of 20 and 30 are drawn to the range and number of jobs that the city offers and the education opportunities that can be found there.
sentences.chinese: 其他所有年龄段的人口迁出数量往往多于迁入数量，而20至30岁的年轻人则被这座城市丰富多样的就业岗位和教育机会所吸引。

sentences.english: This explains why London has one of the youngest average populations in the UK, just 37, according to the BBC.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司称，这也解释了为什么伦敦是英国平均年龄最低的地区之一，仅为37岁。

sentences.english: And the rest of the country?
sentences.chinese: 那么英国其他地区的情况如何呢？

sentences.english: From 2002 to 2015 municipalities such as Liverpool, Birmingham and Manchester saw a population growth of 181%, 163% and 149% respectively, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.
sentences.chinese: 英国国家统计局的数据显示，2002年至2015年间，利物浦、伯明翰和曼彻斯特等城市的人口增长率分别达到了181%、163%和149%。

sentences.english: Young professionals looking for high-paying jobs are attracted to the opportunities provided by growth in sectors such as finance and law.
sentences.chinese: 寻求高薪工作的年轻职场人士，被金融和法律等行业发展所带来的机会吸引而来。

sentences.english: This in turn causes the development of city amenities such as gyms, restaurants and bars, making it an even more attractive place to live.
sentences.chinese: 这反过来又推动了健身房、餐厅和酒吧等城市配套设施的建设，让这些地方变得更宜居。

sentences.english: So are people in the UK leaving cities?
sentences.chinese: 那么英国人是否在离开城市呢？

sentences.english: It depends on where you look.
sentences.chinese: 答案取决于具体地区。

sentences.english: What does seem clear is that people's views on the advantages of urban living may change as they get older.
sentences.chinese: 但有一点似乎很明确：人们对城市生活优势的看法会随着年龄的增长而改变。

sentences.english: Where once was opportunity, now there may be hassle.
sentences.chinese: 曾经充满机遇的地方，如今或许只剩下嘈杂与困扰。

sentences.english: Has your relationship with a city changed over time?
sentences.chinese: 你与一座城市的关系是否也会随着时间而改变呢？
